title: Can living faith separate from charity? Divided vs composed sense
source_text: XXXV. Si quis autem in specie quaerat, An fides viva, quam solam ad salutem & justitiam prodesse concedunt, a charitate separari possit? secundum ipsorum doctrinam per distinctionem quandam respondendum est. Nam in sensu diviso a charitate separari potest, id est, fieri potest, ut fides quae viva est a charitate separetur, & sic non amplius viva, sed mortua sit. Sed in sensu composito fides viva, quae sola actu salvat & justificat, a charitate non potest separari, quia fides sine charitate viva esse non potest, & ad salutem utilis. Nec ista sunt compatibilia, ut fides viva maneat, & tamen sine charitate existat.
pass_a_gloss: But if someone asks in particular whether living faith, which alone they concede profits for salvation and righteousness, can be separated from charity: according to their doctrine one must answer by a certain distinction. For in a divided sense it can be separated from charity — that is, it can happen that faith which is living is separated from charity and so is no longer living but dead. But in a composed sense living faith, which alone actually saves and justifies, cannot be separated from charity, because faith without charity cannot be living and useful for salvation. Nor are these compatible: that faith remain living and yet exist without charity.
pass_b_english: Rome distinguishes: in divided sense living faith can become dead by losing charity.
In composed sense living (=actually saving) faith cannot exist without charity.
